method: Each rectangle was cropped out of the sheet with `niers img crop`, scaled to a tile with
`niers img resize`, assembled into a contact strip with `niers img composite`, and looked at.
A probe was kept only once the tile showed the intended material and nothing else worth
mentioning. Four of the first ten placements were wrong on inspection and were moved.
No image was generated: every pixel here comes from the author's own sheets.

background_rejection.problem: The first rejection rule was generic: light and unsaturated means paper. It ate the character's palest hair, which sits about 0.017 of Oklab from the paper, and the probe then returned the ink outline (#1c150d at 32 %).
background_rejection.fix: The background is measured on each sheet's own four corner patches and rejection is a 0.010 Oklab radius around that measured colour. Measured paper of both sheets: #ece8e6.
background_rejection.effect: hair_pale went from #1c150d at 32 % to #ffede3 at 96 %, and skin from #d2bdb1 at 42 % to #ecd6c9 at 99 % — the old rule had been eating the lit half of the skin too.

measured_2026_09_11.note: The two iris probes are the loose ones, as predicted: the iris is 34 px tall and holds four colours. Every other probe is above 0.68.

Its `share` and `spread` in the run report are the numbers to check first.
